post.description:
Given a job request payload, creates a new job under an existing project and returns new jobId and created status in response 

Note: Make sure projectId matches an existing project to successfully create the job for that project 

Parameters: 

  - jobInstanceName and projectName are accepted as strings (both optional) 

  - jobInstanceName overrides projectName for naming jobs 

  - passing only projectName creates jobs named:   '{projectName}_{total_users}\_users\_{timestamp}' 

  - rampTime and simulationTime are accepted as time strings i.e 60s, 12m, 24h 

  - stopBehavior is matched against accepted values ( END_OF_STEP,  END_OF_SCRIPT,  END_OF_SCRIPT_GROUP,  END_OF_TEST ) 

  - vmInstance matches against AWS EC2 Instance Types i.e m8g.large, m8g.xlarge, etc 

  - workloadType can be set to increasing (linear workload) or standard (nonlinear workload)  

  - targetRampRate, targetRatePerAgent, and jobRegions.percentage fields apply to standard workloadType jobs (nonlinear) 

  - projectId, userIntervalIncrement and numUsersPerAgent are accepted as integers 

  - jobRegions.regions correspond to AWS regions in lowercase i.e us-west-2, us-east-2 

  - jobRegions.users and jobRegions.percentage are accepted as integer strings i.e "100", "4000"

post.description:
Given a project request payload, creates a new project and returns projectId and created status in response on success 

**Note**: Make sure you provide a new project name in request to avoid conflict 

Parameters: 

  - name, productName, comments, and variable key/values are accepted as strings 

  - rampTime and simulationTime are accepted as time strings i.e 60s, 12m, 24h 

  - location, workloadType, stopBehavior, and terminationPolicy are matched against the schema (see corresponding keys in schema) 

  - userIntervalIncrement and dataFileIds are accepted as an integer and a list of integers (datafile IDs to add to project) 

  - testPlans, scriptGroups and scripts are matched against the schema - if testPlans is left empty or excluded from payload, the project defaults to an empty 'Main' test plan with 100% User Percentage 

  - testPlans, scriptGroups and scripts are added in the order in which they appear in the payload; their position is determined by their list index 

  - jobRegions.regions correspond to AWS regions in uppercase i.e US_WEST_2, US_EAST_2 

  - jobRegions.users are accepted as integer strings i.e "100", "4000"

Parameters: 

  - name, productName, comments, and variable key/values are accepted as strings (can be same name as original project, but new variable k/v are added to variable list) 

  - rampTime and simulationTime are accepted as time strings i.e 60s, 12m, 24h 

  - location, workloadType, stopBehavior, and terminationPolicy are matched against the schema (see corresponding keys in schema) 

  - userIntervalIncrement and dataFileIds are accepted as an integer and a list of integers (datafile IDs to add to project) 

  - testPlans, scriptGroups and scripts are matched against the schema, and if there are any entries in testPlans,     it will  **overwrite** the existing test plans - passing an empty list of test plans or excluding it from the payload will keep the current test plans as is 

  - testPlans, scriptGroups and scripts are added in the order in which they appear in the payload; their position is determined by their list index 

  - jobRegions.regions correspond to AWS regions in uppercase i.e US_WEST_2, US_EAST_2 

  - jobRegions.users are accepted as integer strings i.e "100", "4000"

post.description:
Creates a new Tank script through either script file upload or copying an existing script. 

 Tank Script Upload (default): 

        curl -v -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -F "file=@<filename>" 'https://{tank-base-url}/v2/scripts' 



        gzip <filename>

        curl -v -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' -F "file=@<filename>.gz" 'https://{tank-base-url}/v2/scripts'



Tank Proxy Recording Upload: 

        curl -v -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -F "file=@<filename>" 'https://{tank-base-url}/v2/scripts?recording&id=<scriptId>&name=<script-name>' 



        gzip <filename>

        curl -v -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' -F "file=@<filename>.gz" 'https://{tank-base-url}/v2/scripts?recording&id=<scriptId>&name=<script-name>' 

Creating a copy of an existing script: 

        curl -v -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 'https://{tank-base-url}/v2/scripts?copy&sourceId=<scriptId>&name=<script-name>' 

Notes: 

  - **Tank Script Upload**: Only accepts Tank script XML files for an existing Tank script to update. The script ID and script name defined in the first few lines of script XML file should match an existing script entry in Tank to update that script, but setting the script ID to 0 will create a new script with any name.

 - **Tank Proxy Recording Upload**: Only accepts the XML script file recorded and produced by the Tank Proxy Package (see Tools tab in Tank), setting id to an existing scriptId will overwrite that script, both scriptId and name parameters are optional. productName sets the script's product, and filterIds applies those script filters to the recording, in order 

  - **Copying**: You must pass a value for the name parameter to successfully create a copy of an existing script.
